column1: # Every artifact row (`module`, `bytes`) is a wire artifact a conforming
# consumer must REFUSE, paired with the trust-ir verdict that names why and
# with the file where the "consumer MUST" sentence lives (that file cites
# `refuse/<row>` back; scripts/check_enforcement_links.py rule R checks both
# directions). A `none` row is an obligation the corpus CANNOT express as a
# refusable artifact; it exists so the document stating it is held to say so.
# Row ids name the FEATURE, never a wire version (names_not_numbers.rs).
# Carriers: `module` (decodes; refused at a named entry point), `bytes`
# (poisoned wire the reader refuses), `control` (decodes; a conforming
# consumer must ACCEPT it — the envelope every module row shares, the
# identity function under the structural license
# `trust-direct-lane-structural` on the canonical target, which a consumer
# recognizes FOR THE RUN; refuse.rs "The runner is reason-blind"), `none`
# verdicts: `<entry-point>=<verdict>;...`. Entry points (the closed list is
# admission whose Box validity evidence floor is `NamedPremise`),
# admission whose Box validity evidence floor is `ConsumerRederived`),
# validate_module_as_decoded (against the blob's own header version),

column6: why
`Some(BodyGate::Ungated)` is an affirmative claim that no gate was applied to the body; a codegen consumer must refuse it while the structural pass accepts it

a bodied function with no licensing claim in a contract-surface (v41+) blob: the decoded-provenance layer refuses the producer, and the codegen gate refuses the unlicensed body under its fail-closed default (a grandfathering consumer permits it under UnlicensedBodyPolicy::Permit, by name)
a `Gated` authority no consumer recognizes; the policy-free gate leaves recognition to the consumer, and a consumer naming its recognized set refuses it by name
the evidence-bound `clean-kernel-tv` authority worn with no kernel-rechecked TranslationValidation certificate

a kernel-TV license whose `GateEvidence` cites the body's genuine Certified TranslationValidation row but records a body digest that is not the body's: the license was granted to another body (a rewrite after mint, or a transplant); a present evidence is recomputed on every lane, never taken on faith

a genuinely certified kernel-TV license with NO `GateEvidence` recorded: the default lanes admit it (`None` is the pre-evidence meaning), and a consumer that requires the license to name its obligation and body refuses it by name

the envelope every module row shares (the identity function under the structural license on the canonical target) with NO subject: a conforming consumer must ACCEPT it, and one that refuses it has attributed nothing to any row's subject — the license is in no default recognized set, so a consumer names it for the run or fails here by name
a `Gated` license beside a Failed TranslationValidation row about the same body: the license is revoked

module-level `global_asm!` text a consumer cannot lower, check or prove; dropping it silently removes definitions the module may reference, so it must be refused; every projection carries it, text included since WS4.5 (`global_asm "<escaped>"`), so the refusal survives every transport (F-065)

a bare `Dealloc` names neither the owning runtime nor the layout, and the format pins no allocator ABI to lower it to; a conforming backend refuses it in every body and must not recover either from dataflow

a function stamped `Producer::TRust` spells `&mut x` as `BorrowMut`: a Rust producer spells every reference as the place's address or a `Copy` of it and never drives the permission machine, whose never-ended borrows would make every later free of the allocation undefined behaviour (section "A Rust reference carries no permission instruction")
an element op over `Ty::Sequence`, which has no machine layout
a `DialectOp` in a namespace with no registered lowering: well-formed and opaque, unlowerable
a `NoOverflow` claim on the `Assert` that IS the runtime check, with no `ProofRef` to a row about that check: a claim on the check never licenses eliding the check (F-022)

an `Assert` whose panic kind is `Unspecified` (every pre-v52 assert decodes to one): no Rust panic entry point or message to lower a failed check to, so a consumer that lowers panics faithfully refuses it rather than trapping bare (plan item P)
an assert with no panic site has no entry to call and no location to pass, so a faithful consumer refuses it rather than inventing a symbol or trapping (plan item P, amendment P)
an entry that does not take the kind's operands (as `usize`) and then the location would be called with the wrong arguments: a failed check calls `entry(operands.., location)` (amendment P)
a run-time panic location defined as a module global's address: a location known at compile time has one spelling, the static `Global` location (amendment P)
a static panic location naming a mutable global: the panic entry reads the record after the failure, so it must be immutable and not thread-local (amendment P)
an `AssertInvoke`'s unwind edge must enter a landing pad, exactly as an `Invoke`'s must (amendment P)
a `Drop` of a `Struct` with no `drop_glue` row: well-formed, but it states no destructor, so it is never a no-op, neither engine executes it, and no consumer may lower it as nothing (amendment D)
a drop-glue row whose glue is `(i64) -> ()`: drop glue takes exactly one `ptr` (the place) and returns nothing (amendment D)
a direct `call` of a registered drop glue: a destructor runs only through a `Drop` / `DropInvoke`, so every destructor run is a site a verifier can find (amendment D)
a `DropInvoke`'s unwind edge must enter a landing pad, exactly as an `Invoke`'s must (amendment D)
an `InvokeIndirect`'s unwind edge must enter a landing pad, exactly as an `Invoke`'s must (amendment D, Part 2)
a `proved` summary `backed_by` a row of an import: a cross-crate claim the structural pass takes on faith and the authority lane refuses until the dependency is authenticated by digest
`Module.completeness` is `None`: no claim was made, and a consumer that needs a complete module refuses it rather than assuming it
a `Tainted` value consumed by a `TrustedSink`: the module-wide non-interference rule the validator enforces; a consumer lane that skips validation compiles it
an `ObligationKind::Custom` namespace outside the pinned list: the namespace is authority-bearing and is admitted from the pinned list only

an `smtlib2` formula whose `smtlib` rendering is not its payload states two formulas; a consumer must not read either (the contract replay grounded the rendering, so a true rendering was kernel-certified for a false payload)

a function summary clause stating an `smtlib2` payload and a different `smtlib` rendering: one formula holds wherever a module states one, so a caller, a linker or a minted obligation cannot each read a different text

a `requires` clause binding the entry-state pointee (`ParamPointeeEntry`) of a by-value parameter: there is no value behind it, so a consumer that resolved the place would read the clause over memory the signature never names, or over the parameter itself at the pointee's sort

a spec machine's typed invariant carrier stating an `smtlib2` payload and a different `smtlib` rendering (the spec linker compared the rendering and never read the payload, so a Linked machine certified beside a carrier stating another predicate)

a `RefinementType` obligation citing `pred.0` of the module's own predicate table beside a rendering of another predicate: `trust-ir.Pred@1` is a schema trust-ir owns and reads, so the citation and the rendering are two formulas (it validated like its honest twin while the one-formula rule covered `smtlib2` alone)

a declaration renamed out of the namespace with the `<shadowed-by-` marker instead of being dropped: not a link-time symbol, so a consumer that links it emits an undefined reference and one that keys on `display_path` sees two owners of one def
a well-formed enum descriptor on a target whose scalar ABI trust-ir does not tabulate; the lane's alignment is read from the target table, never from its size, and an unknown table is a refusal
a table-backed nominal (`Ty::Dialect`) value created by a raw `Load`: Core rejects every nominal occurrence before machine layout
a well-formed storage geometry carried by value in an unused signature parameter: addressable bytes grant no initialized SSA or ABI value
a `Ty::Handle` naming a runtime absent from the pinned table
a direct `Call` of a bodyless `ExternalWeak` declaration, whose address is nullable
a `Constant::FnDef` of a bodyless `ExternalWeak` declaration: a non-null function item spelling of a nullable symbol
a `Certified` row whose `CleanCic` certificate carries an empty term: nothing for a kernel to re-check, so the kernel tier is not granted
a `SourceProvenance` whose semantic-body digest is not the body's: the carrier is semantic authority and is rechecked, not trusted
two `EnumDef`s with one id
a function whose signature index names no func type
`PtrData` over an `i32`: a pointer op on a type that is not pointer-like
a defined body that writes `*param1` under an effect summary claiming `writes: [*param0]`: a caller that trusted the frame would keep a fact about the written memory across the call

a `Trusted` obligation with the justification the structural pass requires: well-formed, and faith-stamped; the zero-Trusted census (`trust-ir validate --forbid-trusted`) refuses it and a consumer must never read it as kernel-checked
`StructPassingPolicy::Unclassified` beside a by-value struct call: a declaration of absence, not a third convention; a backend needing a classification must refuse rather than pick one
`StructPassingPolicy::AlwaysMemory` beside a by-value struct parameter: every aggregate crossing is pre-lowered (`byval` / `sret` pointers), so the validator refuses the by-value slot

`NativeC` with `pass=indirect` recorded on a two-u64 C-convention struct parameter on aarch64-apple-darwin, which AAPCS64 passes in x0/x1 (clang: `[2 x i64]`): the recorded fact contradicts the placement the consumer computes, and a consumer must refuse rather than prefer either statement
`Unclassified` beside a by-value `Refine(Point, Top)` parameter: a refinement has its base's representation, so this is an aggregate slot and a backend needing a classification must refuse it

`Unclassified` beside a by-value `Vector(I32, 4)` parameter: rustc's Rust ABI passes `int32x4_t` indirectly and `extern "C"` passes it in a vector register, so a producer that classified nothing established neither
`Unclassified` beside a by-value closure with three captures: a closure value carries its captures by value, so this is an aggregate slot and a backend needing a classification must refuse it
`ArgExt::None` on narrow FFI slots on aarch64-apple-darwin: UNRECORDED, never no extension needed; a DarwinPCS consumer must refuse rather than pick one
`CallingConv::CUnwind` on a definition: recorded, never given unwind semantics; a consumer must not treat it as plain `C` where an unwind table matters
`target_features` naming a feature the module's target does not have; a consumer must not compile the body
a `Store` marked `RegionHavocStore`: a backend whose model would treat it as a single-location store must fail closed; translating it as an ordinary store is never sound
an `Undef` marked `FreshSymbolicHavoc` narrowed by an `Assume`: a consumer must independently reject or authenticate any operation that narrows the fresh value
`ArraySplat` at `i32`: `[v; n]` takes `n` from its `Array(e, n)` type, and a non-array type has none
`array[ 7, 7, 7 ]` at `[i32 x 3]`: a uniform array has ONE spelling (`splat[ 7; 3 ]`, SPEC_RATIFICATIONS §3.1), so the list spelling is refused

`switch u8 [ -1: .. ]`: a switch case at an integer selector is a constant of the selector's type (SPEC_RATIFICATIONS §3.3), refused exactly as its `Inst::Const` twin `const u8 -1` is, never wrapped into `255`

`switch i8 [ 255: .. ]`: a switch case at an integer selector is a constant of the selector's type (SPEC_RATIFICATIONS §3.3), refused exactly as its `Inst::Const` twin `const i8 255` is, never wrapped into `-1`

`switch refine<u8, [0, 10]> [ -1: .. ]`: a refinement selector has exactly its base's representation, so its case is a constant of the BASE (SPEC_RATIFICATIONS §3.3), refused exactly as `const u8 -1` is; its own row because a consumer that types a case only at a plain integer selector refuses `switch_case_negative_at_unsigned` and admits this one

`switch usize [ 2^32: .. ]` on wasm32: a pointer-width case is a constant of its selector's type at the TARGET's pointer width (SPEC_RATIFICATIONS §3.3), so `2^32`, the 64-bit spelling of the 32-bit `usize` value `0`, is refused exactly as `const usize 2^32` is there; the row's target is wasm32, so a consumer with no 32-bit lane refuses it for the target too, which a reason-blind runner cannot tell apart

`switch isize [ 2^31: .. ]` on wasm32: above the 32-bit `isize` maximum (the unsigned spelling of `-2^31`), refused exactly as `const isize 2^31` is on the same target, never wrapped; the wasm32 caveat of `switch_case_usize_beyond_target_width` applies

`const usize 2^32` on wasm32: every `isize` / `usize` constant is a value of its type at the target's pointer width (`Constant::value_matches_ty` at `Module::pointer_bits`; 64 bits only for a target-free module), so the funnel refuses the 64-bit spelling the switch-case rows alias through; the wasm32 caveat of `switch_case_usize_beyond_target_width` applies

`not bool %b`: scalar Bool negation spelled with the bitwise `not`; its one spelling is the Bool connective `bxor %b, true` (SPEC_RATIFICATIONS §3.2), so `not` at scalar `Bool` is refused by name (F-033)

one nominal `TypeOrigin` key stamped on two definitions of one module: a key names one source entity, which has one image per module, so a consumer resolving the key has nothing to choose by; refused whatever the two shapes are (the linked-closure form of the same variant needs a root plus a dependency, which one wire artifact cannot carry)
a header in the ambiguous-lineage range (v26..=v28) is refused forever
the magic is not TRUST_IR
the input is cut inside its header: every read is size-checked against the remaining input first, so a short input is TooLarge (and BinaryError::UnexpectedEof is unreachable by construction)
bytes after the canonical payload are refused, never dropped
a declared element count larger than the remaining input is refused before any reservation
a level-S template blob (magic TRUST_IS, amendment S) is not a module: a module consumer refuses it by magic, never instantiates or partially reads it
the template spelling of a type position (Ty tag 39, Ext, then a TemplateRef) under the MODULE magic: refused at every version, because a level-R type has no extension value to read
the template spelling of a constant (Constant tag 17, Ext, then a TemplateRef) under the MODULE magic: refused at every version, as the type tag is
a varint wider than the format admits
a string id past the pool
a pool string that is not UTF-8
a tag the header's version does not allocate (a v40 fat-pointer kind under a v39 header) is refused by name
a genuine direct non-propagating call tag under an older header must be refused instead of interpreted as an ordinary call
a genuine indirect non-propagating call tag under an older header must be refused instead of interpreted as an ordinary call
the entry-state pointee clause place (clause-place tag 10) under a header one version older than its own must be refused, never read as a place that header does not allocate
a consumer unable to enforce an explicit call unwind boundary must refuse even in a function without handlers; capability-dependent refusal cannot be expressed by one universally refusable module
a parameter-attribute flag bit the header's version does not allocate is refused, never dropped

a declared tuple layout whose offsets overlap: the binary reader refuses the incoherent table before any validator sees it, so a consumer validates the complete table by decoding at all (the validator's own `TupleLayoutInconsistent` is reachable only for a hand-built or serde-decoded module)
a PanicLocation byte other than 0 (`Global`) or 1 (`Value`) is refused by name, never read as either (amendment P)
a drop-glue section whose glue ids are not strictly ascending: the table has one order, refused on read before any validator runs (amendment D)
a drop glue IS the source language's destructor for its type: semantics preservation with no refusable module; the rung is the producer's glue oracle (amendment D)

a verdict computed under PanicStrategy::Abort covers panic=abort builds only: a panic=unwind consumer must not rely on it for a function on the unwind surface (one computed under Unwind covers both); a reporting act, not a refusable module (amendment D, Part 2, §21 rule 7)
a consumer must not reassociate a float chain: a semantics-preservation rule with no refusable module; the rung is the bit-exact differential over the consumer's output
consumers must use a present `EnumLayoutDescriptor` instead of the canonical layout: a positive obligation, not a refusal; the rung is differential execution
a 128-bit tag lane's alignment is read from the target scalar table, never its size: a layout obligation, not a refusal; the rung is the layout authority's tests
a consumer must not treat a Lean-envelope fact as bound: a non-inference rule, and a well-formed module must be accepted
while a carrier is deferred a consumer must not infer its meaning from another field: a non-inference rule

a dependency whose digest is not the recorded one must be refused: refusable only from the linked entry point with a root plus dependency PAIR, which one wire artifact cannot carry; the single-module half is `import_backed_summary_unauthenticated`
`site: None` is unbindable, never a wildcard: a well-formed module must be accepted; the obligation is on the consumer's binder
`assurance: None` is NOT RECORDED and a kernel-less consumer fails closed: consumer-internal rules a module cannot exhibit
a run with `host_calls > 0` is host-assisted and must not be presented as in-format evidence: a reporting act, counted on the type
admission consumers must require a matching evidence bundle: needs a bundle sidecar beside the module, which one wire artifact cannot carry
a consumer must not assume the text-loss set is closed: a rule about a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum, not about any module

a consumer that makes a proof claim must not splice an `AvailableExternally` body into a caller unless a `Module.imports` dependency authenticated by `verify_import` exports a structurally equal definition, and keeps the call otherwise: a semantics-preservation premise (the one-definition rule) with no refusable module, since the module is well-formed and must still compile; the rung is the consumer's test

an x86-64 consumer must refuse a vector `ICmp` on a fail-closed `chc_x86` cell (read through `chc_x86_vector_icmp_cell_status`): since 2026-09-28 no covered cell is fail-closed, so no module can land on one; the rung is the reader tests, and a cell that turns fail-closed arrives with a module row that replaces this one
a scalar-pair source argument maps both lanes to the same flattened parameter and omits the other parameter
typed function-pointer ABI pointer width disagrees with the module target
legacy function attributes state zero extension where the typed signature records sign extension
the canonical ABI payload contains an unknown field with unchanged outer framing; the reader refuses instead of dropping it

a signature serde reader must refuse unknown outer JSON/MessagePack map fields instead of erasing a misspelled or future ABI record into legacy absence; the binary-only corpus cannot carry poisoned map keys, so focused reader tests enforce this refusal

a consumer MUST lower a sited assert to a call of its entry and never trap: a lowering obligation no wire artifact can express (the module is well-formed and must compile); the rung is the Trust output gate's failure-path obligation
a frame-bearing function with no entry block cannot seed liveness analysis and must be refused; runtime allocation failures share this diagnostic
a frame handle is closed in its predecessor and closed again after a control-flow edge; the original generation stays dead
a runtime closure provides one capture for its declared two-capture environment
a `tensor<f32, 1>` in an unused signature: a tensor's element must be an integer type, and a float element is refused by name until SemR has a float model (PKG-U15)
a matrix multiply of two `tensor<i32, 2>` operands spelled at `tensor<i32, 3>`: the result rank is the batch axes plus both sides' free axes, so any other rank is refused statically
a well-formed, licensed integer matrix multiply: a tensor contraction has no machine lowering yet (outside the lowering-target subset), so the default codegen gate refuses it by name

the tensor golden under the header one version older than its own, which allocates neither the tensor type tag nor the contraction tag, must be refused, never read as a type or instruction that header does not allocate
a tensor map whose one node reads its own lane: a node reads only the operands and the nodes before it (rule M3), so the body is refused statically, never evaluated
a reduction of a `tensor<i32, 3>` over axes `[2, 0]`: the reduced axes are strictly ascending (rule R2), the one spelling of an axis set, so any other order is refused statically
a view whose result extent reads a result coordinate: the extents are fixed before any coordinate exists (rule V6), so the view is refused statically
a well-formed, licensed map, reduction and view, chained: none has a machine lowering yet (outside the lowering-target subset), so the default codegen gate refuses each by name

the tensor map/reduce/view golden under the header one version older than its own, which allocates the tensor type but none of the map, reduce and view instruction tags, must be refused, never read as an instruction that header does not allocate
a gather of a `tensor<i32, 2>` at one coordinate tensor: a gather takes exactly one coordinate tensor per data axis (rule G2), so the instruction is refused statically, never run

a scatter whose initial tensor is a `tensor<i64, 1>` under the result type `tensor<i32, 1>`: the result starts as a copy of `init`, so `init` has the result type (rule S1), and any other is refused statically, never run
a well-formed, licensed gather and scatter, chained: neither has a machine lowering yet (outside the lowering-target subset), so the default codegen gate refuses each by name

the tensor gather/scatter golden under the header one version older than its own, which allocates the tensor type but neither the gather nor the scatter instruction tag, must be refused, never read as an instruction that header does not allocate

the blob table's one row records the SHA-256 of three `i32` weights but holds those twelve bytes with the last weight changed (rule B2), so the digest the body names is not the bytes it would run on; the constant itself is well-formed
a `tensor_blob` constant whose digest names no row of the (empty) blob table, so the tensor it names has no bytes
a `tensor<i32, 1>` blob constant with extents `[4]` (sixteen bytes) over a row of twelve (rule C4)
a well-formed, licensed weight blob constant: a tensor has no machine layout, so the default codegen gate refuses the `Const` by name
the tensor weight blob golden under the header one version older than its own, which allocates no Constant tag 18: the reader must refuse the constant at its tag
a blob table written in descending digest order: every reader refuses any order but strictly ascending, so each digest is listed once and the table has one byte spelling

a well-formed Box deref fact whose every conjunct is a named premise on param_by_value: the default gates accept it, a floor at the named-premise class accepts it, and a consumer that must not act on a named assumption refuses each conjunct

a well-formed Box deref fact premised on reference_arg_box_valid, a root that says the producing session verified nothing behind it: accepted by default, refused by a consumer that admits only the other roots; the weaker root is a class below, not only a different label
a Box deref whose operand is an i64, not the thin pointer its ptr_ty states
a Box deref of a zero-sized pointee: there is no dereferenceable region to state, and the rule set refuses it rather than admitting it vacuously
a Box deref of an uninhabited pointee: no live allocation of it exists
a Box validity fact with no evidence for Dereferenceable: a missing conjunct is refused, never defaulted
a Box validity fact carrying evidence for NonNull twice
a Box validity fact whose conjuncts are out of canonical order: one fact has one spelling
a sized pointee's fact carrying the wide-only MetadataValid conjunct
a premise that does not name the BoxUnique standing assumption: a premise names every assumption it rests on or is refused
a Box validity fact judged on the optimized fallback body, which is not the body the verifier examined
a Box validity fact that states a session whose verifier did not run: the producer decides validity in its verifier, so no fact of any root or evidence kind exists outside a proof session

null and alignment asserts over the cast result that dominate the load through it: no check shape is admitted, because none is measured against a producer and a target with no route for a failing assert would refuse what the others accept

the result is only observed by ptrtoint, the address is turned back into a pointer by inttoptr and loaded, and the null assert comes after the load: a rule that exempts ptrtoint from the uses a check must dominate would accept an unchecked dereference
a dominating check offered for Dereferenceable: dominating-check evidence is refused in this version, and no check on the pointer value could establish that the allocation is live
an alignment check that claims 4 bytes for a pointee whose ABI alignment is 8: dominating-check evidence is refused in this version
a null check claimed in a function that asserts nothing: dominating-check evidence is refused in this version
both asserts exist over the result, but a load through the result executes before them: dominating-check evidence is refused in this version
both asserts exist and dominate every use, but they test the cast's operand: dominating-check evidence is refused in this version
a Box validity fact citing an obligation row the module does not have: obligation evidence is refused in this version
a Box validity fact citing an Ownership obligation: obligation evidence is refused in this version
a Box validity fact citing a well-formed obligation row of another function, owned by it and sited on its own Box deref: obligation evidence is refused in this version
a Box validity fact citing an obligation sited on another instruction: obligation evidence is refused in this version

a Box validity fact citing a MemorySafety obligation owned by the function and sited on the instruction: obligation evidence is refused in this version, because nothing compares the row's formula with the conjunct
a Box validity fact that omits the allocator non-claim: the fact states everything it does not say or is refused
a premise on an operand defined by null_ptr: the module itself shows NonNull to be false, and a premise the function contradicts is refused, never carried
a premise on an operand defined by inttoptr of a constant: an address made from an integer is not a parameter, an allocation or a returned box
a premise rooted in a by-value parameter of a function that takes none
a premise rooted in an in-body allocation of a body that holds no heap_alloc and no call
a premise on an operand whose Dealloc dominates the deref: the allocation is freed on every path to the instruction
one fact whose premises name two roots: a fact has one root, so a summary by root describes every premised conjunct
a genuine Box deref tag under an older header, which allocates no Inst tag 77, must be refused instead of read
a PremiseRoot byte that names no root is refused by name, never read as any root
